gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's prices for the 14-inch two-screen extenders together with each maker's laptop-fit range and video path. Taken together, these show that Aura's Dual Go 14 Ultra ($319 at us.aura-displays.com, read 2026-11-21) fits 10–16-inch laptops (Aura's range) and needs no driver, because it uses one video output per screen. The Dual Boost 14 ($279, 12–16-inch fit) needs a driver installed. ChatGPT's two-screen pick, the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro ($407.99), is a model that Mobile Pixels' own fit range puts at 15–16-inch laptops.
standout_why: I compared three pages. The cited itechguides 15-best page prices only Amazon no-name extenders and gives no fit range or video path for the Trio. It prices the Trio at Lenovo ($441.99) and never mentions Aura. The cited theofficejournal USB-C page has no prices for its picks and never says whether a model uses DisplayPort Alt Mode or a driver. The top-ranked theofficejournal 14-inch page also gives no prices except an 'under $70' line, says nothing about drivers or DisplayLink, and has no Aura, Mobile Pixels or FOPO model. None of the three gives today's Black Friday prices, and none says which two-screen units need a driver. ChatGPT's own answer shows Aura prices that don't match Aura's store today: cards at $289 and $359, and $389 and $459 in its table.
decides: This changes the two-screen pick. On the size rule (the maker states 14 inches in its fit range), the Trio 3 Pro drops out, because Mobile Pixels' range is 15–16 inches. The Aura Dual Go 14 Ultra meets the rule, has the sharpest panels (2560×1600) and installs no driver, but it needs two video outputs on the laptop. The Aura Dual Boost 14 is cheaper and needs only one cable, but it depends on a driver. Our FOPO S1 and S7 (dual 14-inch, sold as driver-free) cost less than both Auras through our link. They can only take the budget two-screen slot if FOPO's own fit range and per-screen video path are confirmed, and that was not done in this run. The one-screen pick is unchanged: the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS, which takes USB-C Alt Mode or mini HDMI with no driver.
